name: Nu Heru
subtitle: Chondrus crispus sea moss gel with baobab, elderberry and hibiscus, 300 ml or 500 ml
standfirst: A red Chondrus crispus sea moss gel from the cold Atlantic, blended with baobab, elderberry and hibiscus. Sold in a 300 ml or 500 ml glass jar.
body: Nu Heru starts from the same base as the rest of the sea moss shelf: Chondrus crispus, the red seaweed also called Irish moss or carrageen, which grows in cold Atlantic water rather than the warm farmed water some sea moss comes from. To that base the jar adds baobab, elderberry and hibiscus, three plants with a long trade history of their own and a dark red colour that carries through into the gel.

There is no printed iodine figure on this jar, the way there is on Seaking's capsule label, so nothing is claimed about iodine here. Sea moss carries iodine and the amount moves with the harvest, which is exactly why a capsule with a fixed dose is the only format on this site allowed to put a number next to it.
Take it by the spoon, stirred into a smoothie or juice, or into a warm tea with raw honey. Nothing else is added beyond the four named ingredients and the water the gel is prepared with.
spec: One to two tablespoons daily, neat, in a smoothie or juice, or in tea with raw honey
At one tablespoon a day, roughly three weeks from the 300 ml jar and a month from the 500 ml. At two tablespoons a day, about half that

name: Purple Mwani
subtitle: Eucheuma cottonii sea moss gel, warm-water Indian Ocean species
standfirst: A purple sea moss gel made from Eucheuma cottonii, a warm-water species farmed off Zanzibar, Tanzania, in the Indian Ocean. Sold in a single jar size.
body: Mwani is Swahili for sea moss. Eucheuma cottonii is the species most often sold under that name, and it is a different plant to the cold-water Chondrus crispus the rest of this shelf is built from. It grows in warm, shallow Indian Ocean water and is farmed on lines rather than picked off cold-water rock, which is part of why it costs less than the Atlantic jars and why the colour runs to a deeper purple.

As with the other gels on this site, there is no printed iodine figure for Purple Mwani, so no iodine claim is made about it here. If you want a measured number, Seaking prints 75 µg of iodine per capsule.
Use a clean spoon and take it neat or stirred into a smoothie. One tablespoon a day is roughly a 20 day jar, two tablespoons a day roughly ten.

name: Northern Soul
subtitle: Chondrus crispus gel with a blend of four ocean algae, 300 ml or 500 ml
standfirst: A Chondrus crispus gel from the cold Atlantic, wild harvested, carrying a blend of four ocean algae from three families. 300 ml or 500 ml, prepared with water only.
body: The base of the jar is Chondrus crispus, the cold-water red seaweed also called Irish moss or carrageen, picked by hand off Atlantic rock rather than grown in a warm farmed lagoon. Through it runs a blend of four ocean algae from three families, grouped by pigment: red, brown and green.

The gel carries no printed per-spoon iodine figure, because the amount moves with the harvest, so no iodine claim is made on this page. Seaking, the capsule version of this formula, prints a measured 75 µg of iodine per capsule if that number matters to you.

Take one tablespoon each morning, on an empty stomach, straight off the spoon and chased with water, or stirred into tea with raw honey, or blended into a smoothie. It is prepared with water and nothing else.

name: Seaking
subtitle: Chondrus crispus, bladderwrack, kelp, chlorella and clove capsules, 50 x 800 mg
standfirst: The Northern Soul sea moss formula in capsule form: Chondrus crispus, bladderwrack, kelp, chlorella and clove, in 50 vegan capsules of 800 mg. The only sea moss product on this site with a printed iodine figure.
body: Seaking is the capsule version of the Northern Soul blend: Chondrus crispus, Syzygium aromaticum (clove), Fucus vesiculosus (bladderwrack), Laminariales (kelp) and Chlorella, encapsulated at 800 mg per vegan capsule, 50 capsules to a pack.

Each capsule is measured at 75 µg of iodine, and two capsules provide 150 µg. Iodine contributes to normal thyroid function and to normal energy-yielding metabolism. 150 µg is the printed adult reference intake, so two capsules a day meets it in full. Do not exceed two capsules a day.
Take two capsules each morning with at least 500 ml of water. At two a day, a pack of 50 lasts 25 days.

name: Chondrus Crispus
subtitle: Chondrus crispus sea moss gel with Omega DHA oil
standfirst: A plain Chondrus crispus gel, the cold-water Atlantic species also called Irish moss or carrageen, prepared with water and Omega DHA oil. Sold in a glass jar.
body: This is the plain version of the shop's cold-water sea moss: Chondrus crispus on its own, not blended with the other algae in Northern Soul. It is the same species that carries the name Irish moss and carrageen in the old herbals, and it is a different plant to the warm-water Eucheuma cottonii sold here as Purple Mwani.

The gel is prepared with water and Omega DHA oil, and nothing else is added. There is no printed per-spoon iodine figure, so no iodine claim is made here. Seaking, the capsule formula, prints a measured 75 µg per capsule.

Take one tablespoon daily, preferably in the morning on an empty stomach, either raw by the spoon and chased with water, stirred into tea with raw honey, blended into a smoothie, or worked through soup.
